subject: Computer Networking
title: Incident Response Plans
description: A quick win: understand Incident Response Plans.

hook.text: A breach is discovered at 2 AM. Who do you call? What do you shut down? Without a plan, panic takes over.

buildup.text: An incident response plan defines roles, communication chains, and steps for containment, eradication, and recovery.

discovery.text: Tabletop exercises simulate breaches. Teams practice decisions risk-free so they're ready when it counts.

twist.text: Companies that rehearse respond faster and lose less. Those without plans average 287 days to detect a breach.

climax.text: After containment, a post-mortem identifies root causes and improves defenses. Every incident is a lesson.

punchline.text: A plan you practice beats a plan that gathers dust.

quiz.question: What is a tabletop exercise in incident response?
options: A simulated breach scenario to practice response decisions
A physical inspection of server hardware
A method of encrypting backup tapes

details.summary: An incident response plan defines the roles, procedures, and communication channels an organization follows when a security breach occurs. Plans typically cover preparation, identification, containment, eradication, recovery, and lessons learned.
details.whyItMatters: Organizations without incident response plans make costly mistakes during the chaos of a breach. A tested plan reduces response time, limits damage, and ensures legal and regulatory obligations are met.
takeaways: Plans define roles, procedures, and communication for breaches
The six phases cover preparation through lessons learned
Tabletop exercises validate the plan before a real incident

faq.question: What are the phases of incident response?
faq.answer: Preparation establishes the team and tools. Identification detects and confirms the incident. Containment isolates affected systems to stop spread. Eradication removes the threat from the environment. Recovery restores normal operations.

faq.question: What is a tabletop exercise?
faq.answer: A tabletop exercise walks the incident response team through a simulated breach scenario in a discussion format. Participants describe how they would respond at each stage. This reveals gaps in the plan, unclear responsibilities, and missing tools without the pressure of a real incident.
